description:
The same protocol (prove with `Facts.check`, record the strip row with `srec_proven`, choose checked or raw C, `note_bounds`) is written three times: store ~L1004-1018, load ~L1852-1882, word load ~L3286-3297, with three row kinds and note shapes. A fourth access kind would be a fourth copy. Narrow-store verdicts (`narrowed/2`, `int_stored/2`) are noted with `note_fit` but tests read them from C.

Settled shape (grilling 2026-10-19):
- `access(kind, a, i, w, env)` proves, records the strip row and notes the verdict; returns `{proven?, c}`; each site keeps only its C template.
- The three note texts stay unchanged, so the report tests stay byte-identical.

Tests: element_types_test ~L365-368 and word_loads_test ~L160-162 read `notes(:bounds)` and the fit note instead of grepping `defk_to_i16(` / `defk_u64_le_at(`.

Gate: byte-identical `mix dump_c`; `mix ci`; PR per AGENTS.md. Compiler map: "element types" and "statements" rows.
title: One element-access decision instead of three (store, load, word load)
